```{r setup, include=FALSE}
fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", as.integer(yrs[i_pk]), ")")
}

entry_sub_ids <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
  s <- subregion_lookup[[e$key]]
  if (is.null(s)) "western_cape_voc_colony" else s
}, character(1))

zone_entries <- setNames(lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- all_entries[entry_sub_ids == sid]
  pks <- vapply(sub, function (e) max(as.numeric(unlist(e$population))), numeric(1))
  sub[order(-pks, vapply(sub, function (e) e$name, character(1)))]
}), subregion_order)

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- iso3_map[[as.character(e$country)]]
    if (is.null(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(iso_code, ": ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]))
    data.frame(
      Settlement = as.character(e$name),
      Location = loc_str,
      `1700` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1700),
      `1800` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1800),
      `1850` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1850),
      `1875` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1875),
      `1890` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1890),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
bench_nums <- c(1500, 1700, 1800, 1850, 1875, 1890)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates and multi-period population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across eight Southern African countries between 1500AD and 1902AD. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate towns, royal capitals, mission stations, Boer republic seats, stone-walled Tswana *merafe* and colonial ports (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate records excluded), the retained entries span ten historical sub-regions from the Western Cape to Matabeleland, Ovamboland and the lower Zambezi. Active interpolated sites grow from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1500"]], 0L)` in 1500AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1700"]], 0L)` in 1700AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1800"]], 0L)` in 1800AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1850"]], 0L)` in 1850AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1875"]], 0L)` in 1875 and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1890"]], 0L)` in 1890, tracing the shift from indigenous capitals such as Shoshong (26,4k), Kaditshwene (18,4k) and Dithakong (16,8k) to colonial ports and mining hubs led by Johannesburg (102,1k in 1896), Durban (68k in 1900), Cape Town (51,3k in 1891), Port Elizabeth (33k), Pretoria (33k) and Kimberley (28,7k).

# Background

Assembling a unified urban ledger for Southern Africa from 1500AD to 1902AD requires bridging distinct documentary and archaeological traditions. Along the Cape Colony and Natal littoral, Dutch VOC *opgaafrollen* and British municipal census returns provide regular headcounts for administrative towns and mission villages [@Shell1994ChildrenBondage; @Catalog1800StatisticalRegister; @Vink2019FromThe]. Across the interior plateaus of the Highveld, Bechuanaland, Zululand, Lesotho and Zimbabwe, urban scale is attested instead through nineteenth-century traveller itineraries, missionary journals and archaeological surveys of dry-stone compounds and royal *amakhanda* barracks [@Gulbrandsen1993TheRise; @Pikirayi2001ZimbabweCulture; @SAHRIS2024SouthAfrica; @NMMZ2022ZimbabweSites]. Uniting those sources under uniform spatial bounds exposes the demographic transition from pre-colonial Tswana and Rozvi agro-towns to late nineteenth-century mining and railway centres [@Barrow1801AccountTravels; @Smith1849IllustrationsThe].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Sub-Regional Partition

Candidate localities were compiled from colonial blue books, Cape archives, missionary station returns and regional archaeological registers [@Catalog1800StatisticalRegister; @SAHRIS2024SouthAfrica; @NMMZ2022ZimbabweSites]. Within the `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$total_area_km2, 0L)` km² study domain bounded over geoBoundaries outlines [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], `r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate orthographies and overlapping historical records were merged, retaining `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` dated observations. Each settlement is assigned to one of ten historical sub-regions (161 within the 0,25-degree polygon mask plus Massangano-Zambezi and Manyikeni assigned to the neighbouring Rozvi-Mashonaland division).

## Site-Specific Population Estimation

All `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` entries record city-proper limits (163 city-proper, 0 metro) grounded in enumerated census returns, missionary residence tallies or mapped compound footprints [@LaCroix2016KhoikhoiPopulation; @ElphickGiliomee1989Shaping; @Deflem2022WarfarePolitical]. Tables 1 to 10 present linearly interpolated populations at five benchmark years (1700, 1800, 1850, 1875 and 1890) alongside each settlement's exact peak population and peak year, leaving pre-foundation and post-abandonment benchmarks marked by a hyphen (-).

# Testing and Validation

Across the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements, ordinary least-squares rank-size regression on the upper half (`r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$rank_size$n_fit, 0L)` sites) produces a Zipf exponent of $q = 0,89$ ($R^2 = 0,98$; full-sample $q = 1,13$, $R^2 = 0,93$; Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank}). Screening eliminates duplicate colonial and indigenous toponyms while preserving historical continuity across renamings such as Mangaung (Bloemfontein) and Ulundi (Ondini) [@Leanya2024ChurchAnd; @Deflem2022WarfarePolitical].

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Zipf rank-size curve across 163 settlements (q = 0,89, R² = 0,98) and mean sub-regional density in 1900AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.38\\textheight")
)
```

# Results

## Western Cape and VOC-British Heartland

Table \ref{tab:sub-western-cape} records `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["western_cape_voc_colony"]]), 0L)` settlements across the Western Cape, Boland and Namaqualand copper margin, tracing Cape Town, Stellenbosch, Paarl, Worcester, Oudtshoorn and Swellendam alongside early Khoikhoi polities at Cochoqua Kraal and Hessequa [@LaCroix2016KhoikhoiPopulation; @Guelke1976FrontierSettlement].

```{r tab-western-cape, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["western_cape_voc_colony"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the Western Cape and VOC-British Heartland (1500AD to 1902AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-western-cape")
)
```

## Eastern Cape Frontier, Xhosa and Transkei

Table \ref{tab:sub-eastern-cape} lists `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["eastern_cape_xhosa_frontier"]]), 0L)` settlements across the Eastern Cape, Karoo margin and Transkei, led by Port Elizabeth, Grahamstown, King Williams Town, East London and Graaff-Reinet [@Barrow1801AccountTravels; @Catalog1800StatisticalRegister].

```{r tab-eastern-cape, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["eastern_cape_xhosa_frontier"]]),

  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-eastern-cape")
```

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this settlement gazetteer. First, 39 of the 163 settlements possess single-date entries, so benchmark columns outside their attested occupation display a hyphen (-). Second, Cape Town's 1850 synthesis outlier of 290k derives from regional Cape Colony urban compilations and contrasts with municipal headcounts of 21.840 in 1840 and 28.457 in 1865 [@Catalog1800StatisticalRegister; @Shell1994ChildrenBondage]. Third, gazetteer sums represent nucleated urban and royal settlements rather than full rural populations, which are reconstructed in the companion literature review.

# Conclusion

Together, the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements trace four centuries of Southern African urbanisation across eight modern states, charting the transition from Rozvi stone citadels, Tswana *merafe* and Zulu *amakhanda* to the Cape-Natal ports and diamond-and-gold cities of 1902.

# Appendix

## Sub-Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-summary} sums site counts and linearly interpolated settlement totals across all ten historical sub-regions at six benchmark years between 1500AD and 1890AD.

```{r tab-appendix-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- zone_entries[[sid]]
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0(sub_by_id[[sid]]$name, " (", viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L), ")"),
    `1500AD` = sums[["1500"]],
    `1700AD` = sums[["1700"]],
    `1800AD` = sums[["1800"]],
    `1850AD` = sums[["1850"]],
    `1875` = sums[["1875"]],
    `1890` = sums[["1890"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0("All Subregions (", viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L), ")"),
  `1500AD` = tot_sums[["1500"]],
  `1700AD` = tot_sums[["1700"]],
  `1800AD` = tot_sums[["1800"]],
  `1850AD` = tot_sums[["1850"]],
  `1875` = tot_sums[["1875"]],
  `1890` = tot_sums[["1890"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Individually assessed site counts and combined interpolated populations across ten Southern African sub-regions (1500AD to 1890AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:gazetteer-summary")
)
```

# Footnotes

Linear interpolation is bounded strictly between each settlement's earliest and latest observed dates; pre-foundation and post-abandonment benchmarks are left blank with a hyphen (-). Coordinates use European decimal commas in southern and eastern hemispheres (latitude, longitude).
